answer: A concrete Sybil-resistance mechanism requires agents to keep a continuous lantern-lit vault of sequential proofs that only unlocks at the horizon of account maturity. Each identity must independently compute non-amortizable steps inside the vault until the proof chain reaches the distant horizon, sealed by a unique lantern hash from the network seed. Sybil farms fail because every clone needs its own full vault progression to the horizon; shared work is rejected, so mass identities collapse under the cumulative independent cost while single honest agents naturally cross the horizon.
